raw_response:
I have farmed this land in Quzhou for 40 years, and I do not fix what is not broken. Last year my wheat on the big plot gave me about 950 jin per mu, and the summer maize after it gave about 1,000 jin per mu. The cotton on my 4 mu plot was only around 450 jin per mu because the bollworm came late and I did not spray enough times. This year I am keeping the same layout: 12.9 mu for wheat-maize double cropping and 4 mu for cotton. I thought about renting more land, but at 64 years old I do not need the trouble.

For the winter wheat, I will plant the improved Jimai variety that my neighbor Old Zhang used last year — he got over 1,000 jin per mu and the grain buyer paid a good price. I hire the rotary tiller to prepare the field before sowing in early October. For fertilizer, I put 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, then top-dress with urea at jointing stage. All together that is 16 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I would rather put a little too much than risk losing yield; a bad harvest means my grandson’s school fees are in trouble, but wasting a few jin of fertilizer is just a cost. I irrigate three times with my well: once after sowing if the rain does not come, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I spray pesticide twice, mainly for aphids and powdery mildew. I expect 500 kg per mu.

For the summer maize, I plant a hybrid variety right after wheat harvest using the no-tillage seeder from the machinery service. It costs me 40 yuan per mu but saves three days of labor, and at my age I cannot turn the soil by hand anymore. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at sowing and then spread urea when the plants reach knee height. That comes to 14 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once if June is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. Two pesticide sprays for the corn borer. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For the cotton on the 4 mu, I plough deeply first because cotton roots need loose soil down deep. I plant improved Bt cotton seed. The input dealer told me cotton eats a lot of potassium, so I put 8 kg of potassium per mu along with 12 kg nitrogen and 5 kg phosphorus. I irrigate twice, at flowering and when the bolls are swelling. I learned my lesson last year, so this year I spray four times for worms and aphids. I expect 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

My son and daughter-in-law work in Shijiazhuang and send money home, so I have cash to buy inputs, but I still count every yuan. The well means I do not fear drought, but electricity for the pump is expensive, so I do not water more than I need.
